required_tools.name: Octagon lock nut wrench for the fork damper

required_parts.name: Fork oil
required_parts.purpose: 5W fork fluid, about 380 cm³ per leg.

critical_stop_conditions: Oil volume not the same in both legs: correct before riding.
Oil volume below the minimum: rebound damping near full stroke is lost; do not ride.
Front brake lever soft or the caliper dragging after refit: do not ride.
Fork legs not at the same height or not parallel: correct before riding.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Fork oil is replaced every 9 races (about 22.5 hours of riding) and after the first break-in ride. Write down the compression and rebound clicker positions on both legs (count clicks in to the stop, then return), the date and hours.
verification: Clicker positions and hours written down.

steps.title: Wash the fork
steps.instruction: Wash the fork tubes, the bottom of the legs and the clamps, so no dirt gets inside when the fork is opened.

steps.title: Take off the front bodywork and handlebar
steps.instruction: Remove the front number plate and the front disc cover. Peel off the handlebar pad. Remove the handlebar lower holder nuts and washers and lift the handlebar assembly off with its bushings; lay it back on a rag without kinking the cables or the brake and clutch hoses.
verification: Plate, disc cover and handlebar off, hoses not kinked.

steps.title: Free the front brake
steps.instruction: Remove the brake hose clamp bolts and clamps and the fork protector bolts and protectors. Remove the two front caliper mounting bolts and slide the caliper off the disc. Hang the caliper on a strap, never by its hose, and do not pull the brake lever while it is off.

steps.title: Loosen the top clamp
steps.instruction: Loosen the top bridge pinch bolts on both legs.

steps.title: Take out the front wheel
steps.instruction: Put a stand under the engine so the front wheel is off the ground. Remove the axle nut, loosen the left and then the right axle holder pinch bolts, hold the wheel and pull the axle. Take the wheel out and keep the left and right collars with it.

steps.title: Crack the fork damper loose
steps.instruction: With the leg still clamped in the bottom bridge, loosen the fork damper (the cap at the top of the leg) with the octagon lock nut wrench. Only loosen it; do not unscrew it yet.
verification: Damper cap loosened in both legs.

steps.title: Remove the fork legs
steps.instruction: Hold each leg, loosen the bottom bridge pinch bolts and slide the leg out downwards.

steps.title: Open the outer tube
steps.instruction: Hold the outer tube and unscrew the fork damper from it. Do not take the damper out of the leg. Let the outer tube slide down slowly until the dust seal rests on the axle holder.
verification: Damper unscrewed, outer tube down on the axle holder.

steps.title: Drain the oil
steps.instruction: Pump the outer tube up and down several times over a drain pan to push the oil out of the outer tube. Take the O-ring off the fork damper. Turn the compression and rebound adjusters counterclockwise to full soft. Stand the leg upside down over the pan to drain, and note the time and the air temperature.
verification: Oil drained, adjusters at full soft, draining time and temperature noted.

steps.title: Work out how much oil to put back
steps.instruction: Some oil always stays inside. At about 20°C (68°F) the amount left after standing upside down is: 5 min 17.4 cm³, 10 min 15.0 cm³, 20 min 13.7 cm³, 35 min 12.6 cm³, 55 min 11.5 cm³, 85 min 10.5 cm³, 145 min 9.1 cm³. It is a little more when colder and a little less when warmer. Oil to pour in = 380 cm³ (the standard amount per leg with the standard spring) minus the oil left inside. Both legs must get exactly the same amount.
verification: Fill amount worked out for each leg.

steps.title: Choose the oil volume
steps.instruction: Standard is 380 cm³ per leg. The volume can be set from 323 cm³ to 410 cm³ (standard spring) in 5 cm³ steps: more oil makes the fork stiffer near the end of its travel and stops bottoming, less oil makes it softer at the end of the stroke. Never go below the minimum, or rebound damping near full stroke is lost. More oil also makes air pressure build faster while riding.
verification: Oil volume chosen, same for both legs.

steps.title: Fill
steps.instruction: Pour the calculated amount of 5W fork fluid into the outer tube of each leg, measured in a graduated cylinder. Fit a new O-ring, lightly oiled with fork oil, onto each fork damper.
verification: Same measured amount in both legs, new O-rings fitted.

steps.title: Close the outer tube
steps.instruction: Pull the outer tube up slowly and screw the fork damper into it by hand with the lock nut wrench, just snug for now.
verification: Damper started in the outer tube.

steps.title: Refit the legs
steps.instruction: Slide each leg into the clamps and tighten the bottom bridge pinch bolts to 20 N·m to hold it. Tighten the fork damper to 76 N·m with the lock nut wrench. The lock nut wrench lengthens the torque wrench, so set the wrench lower than the actual torque to allow for it (use a beam type torque wrench and work out the correction for the extension).

steps.title: Reset the clickers
steps.instruction: Turn the compression and rebound adjusters back to the positions you wrote down.
verification: Clickers back to the recorded positions on both legs.

steps.title: Set the fork height and torque the clamps
steps.instruction: Loosen the bottom bridge pinch bolts again. Turn each outer tube so the plug bolt faces forward and line up the groove on the outer tube with the top surface of the top bridge. Tighten the bottom bridge pinch bolts to 20 N·m and the top bridge pinch bolts to 22 N·m. Do not overtighten the pinch bolts: it distorts the fork tubes.
verification: Both legs at the same height, pinch bolts torqued.

steps.title: Refit protectors and hose clamps
steps.instruction: Fit the fork protectors with new protector bolts at 7 N·m. Clip the brake hose into its clamps and fit the clamps to the protector, lining up the lower ends of the clamps with the hose protector.
verification: Protectors torqued with new bolts, hose clamped.

steps.title: Refit the front wheel
steps.instruction: Clean the axle and axle holder clamping faces. Fit the collars, put the wheel between the legs, grease the axle lightly and push it in from the right side. Line up the end of the axle with the face of the right fork leg. Fit the axle nut and tighten it to 88 N·m while holding the axle. Tighten the left axle holder pinch bolts to 20 N·m. With the front brake on, pump the fork up and down several times to seat the axle and make the legs parallel, then tighten the right axle holder pinch bolts to 20 N·m.
verification: Axle torqued, pinch bolts torqued, legs parallel.

steps.title: Refit the caliper
steps.instruction: Put locking agent on the caliper mounting bolt threads. Fit the caliper over the disc without twisting the hose and tighten the bolts to 30 N·m. Pump the brake lever until it is firm.

steps.title: Refit the handlebar and bodywork
steps.instruction: Refit the handlebar with its bushings and washers and tighten the lower holder nuts to 44 N·m. Refit the handlebar pad and the front number plate and disc cover.

steps.title: Release the fork air
steps.instruction: Front wheel off the ground, fork fully extended: loosen each fork plug bolt to bring the fork to atmospheric pressure, then tighten it to 1.3 N·m.

steps.title: Check before riding
steps.instruction: Pump the front brake and the fork: no leaks at the dust seals or the damper caps, the fork moves smoothly, the brake is firm and does not drag. Check the wear rings on the fork for wear and that their end gaps face rearward.
verification: No leaks, smooth action, brake firm.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the oil volume used in each leg, the clicker positions and the date and hours.

steps.title: Why this matters
steps.instruction: Air trapped in the fork legs heats up and builds pressure as you ride, so the fork gets stiffer through a race. Let it out after practice and between motos, with the fork fully extended.

steps.title: Lift the front wheel
steps.instruction: Put a stand under the engine so the front wheel is off the ground and the fork hangs fully extended. Never release air with weight on the fork.

steps.title: Release fork air
steps.instruction: Front wheel off the ground, fork fully extended: loosen each fork plug bolt to let built-up air out and tighten it to 1.3 N·m. Do this before any fork setting, and after practice and between motos.

steps.instruction: The compression adjuster is on the fork bolt at the top of each leg. Turn it clockwise (towards H) until it stops: that is fully stiff. Then turn it counterclockwise (towards S), counting clicks; the first click is position 1. Standard is 12 clicks out. Never go past 16 clicks from fully stiff (4 clicks per turn): it damages the fork. Always stop on a click, and set both legs the same.

steps.title: Set fork rebound to standard
steps.instruction: The rebound adjuster is on the centre bolt at the bottom of each leg. Turn it clockwise until it stops (fully stiff), then counterclockwise counting clicks from position 1. Standard is 13 clicks out. Never go past 16 clicks from fully stiff. Set both legs the same.

steps.title: Set shock high speed compression
steps.instruction: The high speed compression adjuster is at the upper right of the shock; it is set in turns. It has 4 1/2 turns from stiffest to softest. Turn it clockwise until it stops, then turn it out 2 1/6 turns from fully stiff.

steps.title: Set shock low speed compression
steps.instruction: The low speed compression adjuster is also at the upper right of the shock; it is set in clicks. Turn it clockwise until it stops, then counterclockwise counting clicks from position 1. Standard is 6 clicks out (13 clicks or more of range, 4 clicks per turn). Stop on a click.

steps.title: Set shock rebound
steps.instruction: The rebound adjuster is at the lower right of the shock. Turn it clockwise until it stops, then counterclockwise counting clicks from position 1. Standard is 11 clicks out (17 clicks or more of range, 6 clicks per turn). Use the right size tool and stop on a click.

steps.title: Set the bike to race weight
steps.instruction: Fill the fuel tank up to the bottom of the filler neck and check the engine oil and coolant are at their correct levels. The rider wears full riding gear.
verification: Fuel to the bottom of the filler neck, oil and coolant checked.

steps.title: Measure unloaded
steps.instruction: With a stand under the engine and the rear wheel off the ground, measure straight between these two points: center of left side rear fender bolt to center of drive chain adjuster lock nut. Write it down.

steps.title: Measure with the rider on
steps.instruction: Take the stand away. The rider sits on the seat in normal riding position and bounces the suspension two or three times, then sits still while a helper holds the bike upright. Measure between the same two points again.

steps.title: Work out the race sag
steps.instruction: Race sag = unloaded length − loaded length. With the standard spring it should be 105 mm.

branches.label: Sag 105 mm
branches.condition: On target.

branches.label: Sag off target
branches.condition: Too little or too much sag.

steps.title: Correct the sag with spring preload
steps.instruction: Too little sag: lengthen the spring installed length (less preload). Too much sag: shorten it (more preload). Use the shock spring preload guide, then measure the sag again. The sag can be set within 95–115 mm.

branches.label: Cannot reach the target
branches.condition: The spring length runs out of its adjustment range before the sag is right.

steps.title: Change the spring if needed
steps.instruction: If you cannot get the standard sag inside the adjustment range: too little sag even at the longest length means the spring is too stiff for the rider, so fit the optional soft spring and set the sag to 110–115 mm. Too much sag even at the shortest length means fit the optional stiff spring and set the sag to 95–100 mm.

verification: Test ride done on standard settings.

steps.instruction: Write down every clicker setting, the race sag, the spring fitted, the rider weight and the track conditions.

required_tools.name: Torque wrench with a pin spanner adapter

critical_stop_conditions: Installed length outside its range: fit a different spring instead.
Lock nut not torqued: the adjuster can move while riding.
Shock leaking oil or losing height after riding: have it checked (it may be losing nitrogen).

steps.title: Know why you are changing it
steps.instruction: Spring preload is only used to set race sag; it does not make the spring stiffer. Measure the race sag first (see the suspension baseline guide) and note whether you need more or less sag.
verification: Current race sag and the target written down.

steps.title: Get to the spring adjuster
steps.instruction: Remove the engine guard and the muffler so you can reach the top of the shock spring. Put a stand under the engine so the rear wheel is off the ground and the spring is unloaded.
verification: Muffler off, rear wheel off the ground.

steps.title: Measure the spring installed length
steps.instruction: Measure the length of the spring from seat to seat and write it down. Standard is 230.7 mm (9.08 in).

steps.title: Loosen the lock nut
steps.instruction: Clean the threads on the shock body. Using two pin spanners, hold the spring adjuster and loosen the lock nut above it.

steps.title: Turn the adjuster
steps.instruction: Turn the spring adjuster with a pin spanner: making the spring longer reduces preload (more sag), making it shorter adds preload (less sag). One full turn of the adjuster changes the spring length by 1.5 mm, which is 75 N of preload with the standard spring. With the standard spring keep the installed length within 224.9–231.7 mm. Do not go outside that range: fit a different spring instead.
verification: Spring length set inside the range.

branches.label: Target needs a length outside the range
branches.condition: Fit the optional soft or stiff spring instead of forcing the preload.

steps.title: Tighten the lock nut
steps.instruction: Hold the adjuster with one pin spanner and tighten the lock nut against it to 44 N·m.
verification: Lock nut torqued against the adjuster.

steps.title: Refit the muffler and guard
steps.instruction: Refit the muffler with its sealing and clamps as they came off, tightening the muffler joint band bolt to 10 N·m and the mounting bolts firmly. Refit the engine guard at 10 N·m.
verification: Muffler and guard back on and tight.

steps.title: Check the sag again
steps.instruction: Measure the race sag again with the rider on. Repeat the adjustment until it is on target.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the new installed length, the race sag and the rider weight.

Shock leaking oil or losing height after riding: have it checked (it may be losing nitrogen).

steps.title: Know why you are changing it
steps.instruction: Spring preload is only used to set race sag; it does not make the spring stiffer. Measure the race sag first (see the suspension baseline guide) and note whether you need more or less sag.
verification: Current race sag and the target written down.

steps.title: Get to the spring adjuster
steps.instruction: Remove the engine guard and the muffler so you can reach the top of the shock spring. Put a stand under the engine so the rear wheel is off the ground and the spring is unloaded.
verification: Muffler off, rear wheel off the ground.

steps.title: Measure the spring installed length
steps.instruction: Measure the length of the spring from seat to seat and write it down. Standard is 234.6 mm (9.24 in).

steps.title: Loosen the lock nut
steps.instruction: Clean the threads on the shock body. Using two pin spanners, hold the spring adjuster and loosen the lock nut above it.

steps.title: Turn the adjuster
steps.instruction: Turn the spring adjuster with a pin spanner: making the spring longer reduces preload (more sag), making it shorter adds preload (less sag). One full turn of the adjuster changes the spring length by 1.5 mm, which is 72 N of preload with the standard spring. With the standard spring keep the installed length within 228.0–238.0 mm. Do not go outside that range: fit a different spring instead.
verification: Spring length set inside the range.

branches.label: Target needs a length outside the range
branches.condition: Fit the optional soft or stiff spring instead of forcing the preload.

steps.title: Tighten the lock nut
steps.instruction: Hold the adjuster with one pin spanner and tighten the lock nut against it to 44 N·m.
verification: Lock nut torqued against the adjuster.

steps.title: Refit the muffler and guard
steps.instruction: Refit the muffler with its sealing and clamps as they came off, tightening the muffler joint band bolt to 10 N·m and the mounting bolts firmly. Refit the engine guard at 10 N·m.
verification: Muffler and guard back on and tight.

steps.title: Check the sag again
steps.instruction: Measure the race sag again with the rider on. Repeat the adjustment until it is on target.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the new installed length, the race sag and the rider weight.
